title: MZ What's the point of plugins if I can't access data?

posts.author: Fringo
posts.body:
Hi.
I'm trying to create a plugin. Part of it is an array that contains important data for the game. I cannot seem to create script calls in events that allow me to access that array. I'm aware that's because the data in the script is not global. I can do plugin commands to run specific functions - but I guess I just can't access any data in the script even using other scripts in events? Do I have to assign the array to a $gameVariable.value(), converting it to a useless string, then convert it back? What's the point?

posts.author: Ludovinsky
posts.body: Huh? In MZ, anything you declare inside a plugin is inside the plugin’s private scope, so event Script Calls can’t see it. To access plugin data from events, you have to put that data on a global object.

just to note, this is true if your plugin runs within an IIFE. without one, a variable declared outside of a function's scope would be global.

Fringo said:
Do I have to assign the array to a $gameVariable.value(), converting it to a useless string, then convert it back? What's the point?
Click to expand...
setValue allows you to assign arrays without needing to stringify them, and the assignment is by reference. so anything you'd to to it would happen to the original array and there'd be no need to "convert back". but if the variable was already in global scope there's no need to outside of saving the value to the save file vs letting it reset with the session

variable x should be your array, yes. when setting it, the script call to do so is
$gameVariables.setValue(x, value)
where value is your array. the script call to retrieve the value is
$gameVariables.value(x)
, not
$gameVariables(x)
. you should have gotten an error in the console when using that for it not being a function

No, it's not RPG Maker, that's programming.
In a game, you have more than a simple database where you can SQL-query everything. You have different kind of data:
- Data that loads on game start and lives forever (e.g. BGM volume)
- Data from your disk, e.g. maps, items, skills, classes, initial skills of actors, ...
- Data that lives while on a map, e.g. where your player is, where the events are, how they look like right now...
- Data that lives in your save game, and resets when starting a new game, or loading another save, e.g. switches, variables, selfswitches, members of your party, the levels of your actors...
- ...probably some more
From reading your posts, it looks like you're mixing them up. But it would help us a lot when you would provide a biiiit more information.
